refined_contract.contract: DEV_MODE is an environment-controlled capability gate. Disabled DEV_MODE must prevent DEV handler registration or fail closed before any DEV side effect, according to the authoritative V1 registration path.

DEV_MODE and administrator identity are distinct dimensions. ROM_ADMIN_USER_IDS is evidence for administrative authorization; auction-specific identity sources are separate V1 policy and must not be silently merged without parity resolution.

V2 requires one explicit authorization decision before command execution: capability enabled, caller authorized for the operation class, and command classified as allowed. Existing V1 local checks remain evidence, not automatically canonical duplicates.

The effective register_dev_handlers definition and main.py invocation chain must be identified by Python last-definition semantics. Earlier duplicate definitions are shadow candidates and cannot be treated as simultaneous canonical owners.

Commands must be classified as read-only diagnostics, controlled reversible mutation, destructive reset, or administrative production operation. Test helpers in db_modules/dev_compat.py are not Telegram authorization policy by themselves.

Authorization must complete before database writes, item grants, currency changes, resets, notifications, or other observable side effects. Unauthorized and disabled paths must not partially mutate state.
Where V1 provides durable audit or idempotency, V2 must preserve it. The audit must not invent a universal ledger for commands whose V1 owner has none; gaps require explicit parity resolution.
Configuration variable names may be modeled, but .env values and identity lists must never be copied into reports, tests, documentation, or source defaults.

superseded_policy: Keyword matches outside authoritative owners are not DEV authorization policy.
db_modules/dev_compat.py mutation helpers do not independently authorize callers.
